_comment: Risk-path rule table for forecast. This repo moves no money and ships no
product, so there are no financial rules. Two surfaces carry real risk:
internal/jira writes to a live external system, and the prediction core is
what people size projects against — a wrong number there is silent and is
Semantics are the same everywhere: risk is the MAX over matched rules,
components the UNION, financial an OR, and a file is presentational only if
every rule it matched is. Adding a rule can only ever raise risk.
scaffold is true: this table has not yet been reviewed by a human.

rules.note: internal/jira mutates issues in a live JIRA instance and ingest projects a whole dispatcher run onto them. A defect here is not recoverable by re-running: it has already commented on real tickets.

The simulator, the reference class and the dispatched-work model. Output is a number nobody can sanity-check by eye, so a wrong one is believed and planned against. Not high — it ships no code and gates nothing — but never presentation.
Parsers for JIRA exports, tasks YAML and dispatcher journals. Silent mis-parse becomes silent mis-prediction.
A change here can DISABLE a check rather than fail one, so it is never presentation.
Fixtures encode the assertions the tools are verified against. Weakening one weakens the verification.

gate_signals.note: ingest is dry-run by default and only writes to JIRA behind --apply. Anything touching that boundary decides whether a real external write happens.
Defaults that let missing data read as a valid answer. In a forecaster the canonical form is an absent reference-class cell silently becoming a default distribution.
